CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #5 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The shield and two crossed spears on the flag stand for (1 mark)
   A. sports
   B. farming
   C. defence of freedom
   D. music

2. Leaning far backwards while sprinting will (1 mark)
   A. slow you down like a brake
   B. make no difference
   C. make you faster
   D. make you jump

3. Why should the flag stick be held high when cheering? (1 mark)
   A. To make noise
   B. To block the sun
   C. To hide the runners
   D. So it does not hit anyone

4. The Kenyan flag has stripes of (1 mark)
   A. red, white and blue
   B. blue, yellow and white
   C. orange and green
   D. black, red and green with thin white stripes

5. A good sequence has (1 mark)
   A. no order
   B. only noise
   C. only jumps
   D. a clear start, smooth middle and controlled finish

6. A roll in gymnastics is (1 mark)
   A. a run
   B. a movement in which the body turns over along the floor
   C. a still position
   D. a song

7. In a side roll, your body should be (1 mark)
   A. bent at the waist
   B. hanging in the air
   C. straight and long like a log
   D. curled like a ball

8. Why do we stand up slowly after a side roll? (1 mark)
   A. To make noise
   B. To win a prize
   C. To look tall
   D. To avoid feeling dizzy

9. Dynamics means (1 mark)
   A. the pitch
   B. the words
   C. how loud or soft the music is
   D. the speed

10. In music, the sign p means (1 mark)
   A. loud
   B. fast
   C. soft
   D. stop

11. A song about washing hands to prevent germs is a (1 mark)
   A. funeral song
   B. naming song
   C. topical song
   D. marriage song

12. A patriotic song shows (1 mark)
   A. a rainy day
   B. fear
   C. love of sweets
   D. love for one's country

13. Which light is best for outdoor photographs? (1 mark)
   A. A torch in the eyes
   B. Natural sunlight falling on the subject
   C. Only midday shadows
   D. Darkness

14. What should you do about distracting things behind the subject? (1 mark)
   A. Photograph them too
   B. Add more
   C. Ignore them always
   D. Remove them or change the angle

15. Where must you never take photographs? (1 mark)
   A. At the school gate
   B. In private places such as toilets
   C. In the playground with permission
   D. In the classroom with permission

16. To make the centre of interest clearer you can (1 mark)
   A. move closer to the subject
   B. shake the camera
   C. move very far away
   D. add lots of clutter

17. Which hand is at the top of the recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Left
   B. Neither
   C. Right
   D. Both feet

18. Another name for the descant recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. soprano recorder
   B. drum
   C. bass recorder
   D. xylophone

19. When you make a mistake while playing in a group, you should (1 mark)
   A. shout
   B. stop the whole group
   C. throw your recorder
   D. carry on with the beat

20. For a good tone you should blow (1 mark)
   A. gently and steadily
   B. only in short puffs
   C. as hard as you can
   D. with your cheeks puffed for ever

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. What does singing in unison mean? Why is it good for an anthem? (3 marks)

22. State what the colours black and green stand for on the Kenyan flag. (2 marks)

23. How should you give feedback on a friend's photograph? (3 marks)

24. Describe how to get into a crab balance. (4 marks)

25. State four performance techniques for a good singer. (4 marks)

26. How should we behave towards the national flag? (3 marks)

27. Name the three joints of a descant recorder and state where the mouthpiece is. (3 marks)

28. Name two digital devices used for taking photographs. (2 marks)

29. How can you show the mood of a joyful song when singing? (3 marks)

30. Describe the fingering for B, A and G. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #5 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — defence of freedom
   The shield and spears represent the defence of freedom.

2. A — slow you down like a brake
   Leaning back acts like a brake.

3. D — So it does not hit anyone
   Keeping it high and away from the track avoids hitting people.

4. D — black, red and green with thin white stripes
   The flag has black, red, green and white.

5. D — a clear start, smooth middle and controlled finish
   Good sequences are planned and controlled.

6. B — a movement in which the body turns over along the floor
   A roll turns the body over along the mat.

7. C — straight and long like a log
   A straight, tight body rolls smoothly.

8. D — To avoid feeling dizzy
   Getting up too fast can make you dizzy.

9. C — how loud or soft the music is
   Dynamics are the loud and soft parts.

10. C — soft
   The letter p stands for soft.

11. C — topical song
   It gives a message about a topic of importance.

12. D — love for one's country
   Patriotic songs celebrate the nation.

13. B — Natural sunlight falling on the subject
   Natural light is best.

14. D — Remove them or change the angle
   A plain background keeps attention on the subject.

15. B — In private places such as toilets
   Privacy must be respected.

16. A — move closer to the subject
   Getting closer helps the subject fill the picture.

17. A — Left
   The left hand is at the top and the right hand at the bottom.

18. A — soprano recorder
   The descant is the soprano recorder.

19. D — carry on with the beat
   Continue and rejoin.

20. A — gently and steadily
   A gentle, steady breath gives a warm tone.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone sings the same notes at the same time. It is simple and everybody can join in together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 2 marks for the reason.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Black stands for the people of Kenya. Green stands for the land and its natural wealth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say what you like first, comment on light and centre of interest, and suggest one improvement politely.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sit with knees bent and feet flat. Put hands behind you shoulder-width apart with fingers pointing to the feet. Push through hands and feet to lift the hips so the body is level. Hold for a few counts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Good posture; deep breathing; clear diction; gestures; facial expression; eye contact. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not let it touch the ground, do not write on it, keep it clean and not torn, and stand still and quiet when it is raised.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Head joint, middle joint and foot joint. The mouthpiece is on the head joint.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the joints, 1 mark for order or naming all, 1 mark for the mouthpiece.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Smartphone, tablet, digital camera. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Smile, use lively gestures, sing brightly and at a lively tempo.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: B uses the thumb and hole 1; A uses the thumb and holes 1 and 2; G uses the thumb and holes 1, 2 and 3.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each note.
